{ "reviewId": 5102575402, "state": "COMMENTED", "submittedAt": "2026-09-03T13:35:15Z", "commentCount": 1, "body": " ## Copilot review overview ### 🟡 Changes recommended `load()` can leave stale `cargo` state on failure, which can make a failed load appear partially successful in the view-scoped bean. *Once you've addressed the issues Copilot identified, you can request another Copilot review.* **Review tier:** Lite **Findings:** 1
New issues introduced by this change (1) | Severity | Finding | |:--:|:--| | | `src/​main/​java/​org/​eclipse/​cargotracker/​interfaces/​booking/​web/​ChangeArrivalDeadlineDate.java` — `load()` clears `arrivalDeadlineDate` but not `cargo`. If `loadCargoForRouting(trackingId)` or date… |
What changed in this PR Adds a new JSF view-scoped backing bean to support editing a cargo’s arrival deadline via `BookingServiceFacade`, keeping domain types out of the web layer and surfacing load/update failures as JSF errors. **Changes:** - Introduces `ChangeArrivalDeadlineDate` (`@Named @ViewScoped`, `Serializable`) exposing `trackingId`, loaded `CargoRoute`, and editable `Date`. - Implements `load()` to fetch `CargoRoute` and parse the DTO’s `MM/dd/yyyy` date-only deadline into an editable `Date`, throwing `FacesException` on failures. - Implements `changeArrivalDeadline()` to reject null dates, delegate to `changeDeadline(...)`, and close the PrimeFaces dynamic dialog only on success. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | src/​main/​java/​org/​eclipse/​cargotracker/​interfaces/​booking/​web/​ChangeArrivalDeadlineDate.java | New view-scoped backing model for loading and submitting an edited arrival deadline through the booking facade. |
--- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.", "comments": [ { "id": 3925097563, "path": "[REDACTED].java", "line": 68, "body": "`load()` clears `arrivalDeadlineDate` but not `cargo`. If `loadCargoForRouting(trackingId)` or date parsing fails, the view-scoped bean can retain a previously loaded `cargo`, which can make a failed load look partially successful (stale cargo details rendered with a cleared date). Clearing `cargo` up-front (and on failure) avoids stale state and also lets you differentiate "missing cargo" from "missing arrival deadline" more explicitly." } ] }
